mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future cash flows reduce the present value of expected equity returns, causing a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative after a FEDFUNDS increase >0.25%, or the effect is indistinguishable from zero (p > 0.1) in a 200-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor emplacements) by at least 2% signals strong labor market demand, which raises corporate earnings expectations and drives a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive after a sustained labor growth ≥2%, or earnings revisions remain flat (Z < 1.0) during the period.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP personal consumption) grows faster than CPIAUCSL (CPI) by at least 0.5% monthly, real income growth outpaces inflation, producing a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate by ≥0.5% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive after the divergence, or the divergence is not sustained for ≥3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 3% in a month indicates supply-side weakness, which reduces market confidence and produces a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after INDPRO decline >3%, or the effect is absent in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5% for three consecutive months, the market anticipates continued easing, which elevates equity valuations and drives a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return (always-on signal).
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in the low-rate regime, or the signal is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% triggers a labor market tightening that increases wage growth expectations and supports a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive after UNRATE < 4%, or wage growth revisions are flat.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) increases by at least 10% in the next two months, it signals a resilient housing market and optimistic consumer sentiment, leading to a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥10% over the next two months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive after the housing acceleration, or the effect is not detected in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS (retail sales) below 100,000 thousand dollars indicate weak consumer demand, which depresses earnings expectations and produces a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return (interaction between RSAFS and GDPC1).
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 100,000 for two consecutive months AND GDPC1 growth < 2% for the same period
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after the interaction signal, or the combination is not statistically predictive (p > 0.1).
